name: Sootmark Nightwatch Layer Set
description: Built for staying invisible in the dark industrial corridors of the Shelf while remaining functional in the cold. The base is a full-length thermal underlayer in matte black — the kind of utilitarian piece that Circuit-tier factories produce by the millions, here worn past its intended lifespan, the cuffs replaced with strips cut from a neoprene wetsuit and secured with adhesive seam tape. Over that comes a mid-layer hoodie in deep charcoal fleece, the hood reinforced with a wire brim salvaged from a hard hat so it holds its shape in wind without being pulled back. The hoodie's kangaroo pocket has been subdivided internally with sewn-in elastic loops holding a small flashlight, a multi-tool, and a folded strip of reflective tape for emergencies. The outer layer is a cut-down jacket — originally longer, now cropped at the hip with the cut edge raw and sealed with heat-bond tape — in matte dark olive synthetic ripstop. The back panel has been stenciled in rust-colored paint with a crude geometric sigil, the mark of a specific Shelf block watch rotation. Trousers are slim-cut tactical in faded charcoal, both knees double-layered with iron-on rubber patches. Footwear is a pair of heavy low-profile boots in matte black rubber-composite, the lug soles worn almost flat but retreaded with adhesive grip strips along the ball of the foot for quiet movement on wet metal grating. A neck gaiter in dark gray sits around the throat, doubling as a face cover. Spinal rig aug-compatible: the jacket and hoodie both have a central back channel — a vertical seam left unstitched and finished with snap-close flaps — running from collar to hem.
functionality: Full thermal layering for cold industrial night environments. Hard-hat wire brim keeps hood functional in wind. Internal pocket organizer for essential tools. Jacket back channel accommodates spinal rig augmentation. Grip strips on boot soles enable quiet movement on wet surfaces. Neck gaiter provides respiratory and face protection. Block-watch sigil identifies the wearer to allied residents.
what_it_says: Someone who watches. Patient, organized, community-invested in a specific way — this isn't a loner's outfit, it's a person embedded in a local network. The sigil on the back is a declaration of territory and responsibility. The spinal channel on the jacket suggests a serious aug investment, unusual for Tier 1, and implies either a past in a higher tier or a very specific set of skills that made the hardware worth sacrificing for.
worn_by: former Tier 2 workers who fell through the cracks
manufacturer: Base pieces from Circuit-tier surplus; modifications self-made; sigil stenciled by local block artist
story_hooks: The rust-colored sigil on the jacket back is a block watch mark — but the block it represents was condemned and evacuated six months ago. Why is the wearer still wearing it, and are they the only one left?

The spinal rig channel in the jacket is cut to accommodate a specific military-grade rig configuration that hasn't been available on the civilian market for fifteen years. Someone who recognizes the spec wants to know where it came from.

The internal pocket organizer holds a strip of reflective tape that, when unfolded, reveals handwritten coordinates on the non-reflective backing — coordinates to something the wearer has been guarding the location of for a very long time.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately anonymous, urban sentinel silhouette. The layered set creates a streamlined, almost formless profile in shades of black, charcoal, and muted olive — designed to dissolve into industrial shadows. The reinforced hood and cropped jacket suggest someone built for function over presence. Block artist sigil on the back reads as street-credentialed territory marker.
physical_description.fit: Slim through the core with intentional slack at shoulders for movement freedom. The cropped jacket sits at hip with relaxed sleeves; hood constructed to sit flat against the head without puffing. Tactical trousers taper gently to the ankles, allowing clear lines to the boots. Compression-adjacent through the thermal layer, but the mid and outer layers add just enough volume to move in.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte black synthetic thermal base; deep charcoal fleece mid-layer; matte dark olive ballistic ripstop outer jacket. Black rubber-composite boots. Gray neoprene-hybrid neck gaiter. Heat-sealed seams and adhesive patches throughout.
physical_description.texture: Thermal layer smooth and thin; fleece slightly napped and insulating; ripstop with tight-weave industrial texture. Visible heat-bond tape edges on the cropped hem create subtle ridged lines. Boot soles worn smooth with tactile adhesive grip strips. Raw cut edges on jacket reinforce the salvage aesthetic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Foundation of pure matte black throughout (thermal, boots, gaiter). Mid-layer in deep charcoal (fleece). Outer layer muted olive drab (ripstop). Accent: rust-orange block artist sigil on back panel. Emergency reflective tape hidden in kangaroo pocket (silver-white). Subtle wear-fading on trousers creates shadow-line patterns.
physical_description.closures: Hoodie: standard drawcord with metal aglets; kangaroo pocket secured with interior elastic loop dividers. Jacket: friction-fit cropped cut with no closures by design; central back channel uses snap-flap access for aug-rig compatibility. Neck gaiter: worn loose, no fasteners. Trousers: likely magnetic snap or friction waistband (not specified, assumed standard tactical). Boots: adhesive grip-strip application, lug-sole wear.
distinctive_features: Wire-reinforced hood brim salvaged from hard hat — maintains shape without collar pull
Kangaroo pocket subdivided with sewn-in elastic loops for small tools (flashlight, multi-tool stored ready)
Double-layer knee patches with iron-on rubber application — shows tactical wear prep
Cropped jacket with raw edge sealed via heat-bond tape — visible industrial modification
Central back channel with snap-flap closures for spinal rig augmentation compatibility
Neoprene cuff replacements on thermal layer secured with seam tape — extended lifespan hack
Rust-orange block sigil stencil on back panel — territorial/rotation marker by local artist
Retreaded boot soles with adhesive grip strips on ball-of-foot for silent grating movement
Neck gaiter doubling as emergency face cover — quick deployment design
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage-core, with intentional Tier 3 functional workwear baseline. The modifications and street-artist sigil signal sub-grade territory identification, but the preserved functionality suggests someone operating with discipline and resources (tools, adhesives, contact with local artists). Not luxe, not corporate — this is earned street credibility through careful maintenance of hand-me-down kit.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wears as: Shelf block watcher, industrial maintenance or cargo handler, possibly informal security or territorial infrastructure guardian. The aug-rig compatibility suggests ongoing relationship with subcutaneous or frame mods (Tier 5 typical). The sigil marks tribal affiliation to a specific Shelf rotation. Silent movement on metal grating + tool loop prep = someone who works in the cold dark corridors between megastructures. Not trying to be seen; trying to be functional and unremembered.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately worn and patched, but meticulously maintained. Boots are retreaded (not replaced), indicating resourcefulness. Seams are sealed, cuffs replaced, patches iron-on secure. The raw-cut jacket edge and heat-bond tape are *intentional* design choices, not damage. Overall impression: broken-in and well-loved by someone who knows every pocket, every grip surface, every modification they made themselves.

image_prompt: A lean neo-noir sentinel in layered blacks and muted olive, standing three-quarter profile in a dim industrial corridor lined with corrugated metal. Thermal layer visible at wrists; charcoal fleece hood fits snug against the head with reinforced wire brim holding its shape. Cropped jacket sits at hip with raw heat-sealed edges catching pale overhead light. Rust-colored geometric sigil is faintly visible on the back panel. Neck gaiter loose around throat. Tactical trousers fade to matte black boots with worn tread and visible adhesive grip strips on the soles. One hand rests on the kangaroo pocket, suggesting access to tools. Moody blue-gray ambient light from high industrial fixtures; wet metal grating reflects pale light at floor level. Background blurs into stacked cargo containers and shadow. The figure reads as deliberate, territorial, built for cold and silence. --ar 2:3 --v 6
